items.title: Tourism boom pushes limits of Athens air traffic control
items.summary: GREEN arrows representing tourist-laden jets pile up on the screens of the Athens air traffic controllers, a puzzle to solve at the height of tourist season. exclaimed Olga Toki, vice-president of the Association of Air Traffic Controllers of Greece. There is no doubt that this is a busy summer for the overworked air traffic controllers.

items.title: Shein to pay up to US$3.5bil to select pre-IPO investors around Hong Kong listing
items.summary: They hold Shein's late-stage funding shares - Series pre-D, Series D and Series D plus preferred - which carry protections triggered by an IPO below the prices paid in earlier funding rounds. That is below the private valuations attached to the eligible funding rounds of US$60.5 billion for the Series pre-D round in 2022, US$98.2 billion for the Series D round later that year and US$64 billion for the Series D plus round in 2023. Separately, Shein also agreed to make about US$1.33 billion in payments to holders of Series pre-D, D and D plus preferred shares.

items.title: FMM dismisses MTUC’s RM3,100 minimum wage proposal as unrealistic for businesses
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 24 — The Federation of Malaysian Manufacturers (FMM) has rejected a proposal by the Malaysian Trades Union Congress (MTUC) to raise the national minimum wage from RM1,700 to RM3,100, cautioning that an 82.4 per cent surge is detached from prevailing economic realities. FMM president Jacob Lee Chor Kok said that while the federation supports higher wages as Malaysia strives for high-income status, an abrupt RM1,400 increase in a single revision remains unprecedented. Under the National Wages Consultative Council (NWCC) Act, the next mandatory statutory wage review is slated for February 2027.

items.title: Police review CCTV footage in fatal Putrajaya cycling accident probe
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: Police are reviewing closed-circuit television (CCTV) footage around the scene of an accident in which two cyclists were killed after being hit by a car at Km9.0 of Jalan Persiaran Selatan, Presint 5, here last Thursday. District police chief Assistant Commissioner Aidi Sham Mohamed said the cause of the incident is still under investigation, and police require further verification through the CCTV footage. "Investigating officers will go to the Putrajaya Corporation's Putrajaya Command Centre today to review the CCTV footage from the scene for further action," he said when contacted today.

items.title: Fadhlina receives Datuk Seri title, Ziana Zain now a Datuk
items.summary: Fadhlina will receive the Darjah Gemilang Seri Melaka (DGSM), which carries the title Datuk Seri. Meanwhile, 56 individuals were conferred the Darjah Cemerlang Seri Melaka (DCSM), which carries the title Datuk Wira. Another 189 recipients were conferred the Darjah Pangkuan Seri Melaka (DPSM), which also carries the title Datuk.

items.title: Two Datuk remanded for 3 more days over alleged land abuse
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: The Magistrates' Court here today granted a three-day remand extension for two Datuk, including a Datuk who is a government agency chairman, over alleged abuse of power involving government agency land. Besides the 53-year-old Datuk who chairs a government agency, the other Datuk, in his 40s, is a developer. Three others previously remanded, including the Datuk chairman's brother, sister-in-law and a developer, have been released on bail.

items.title: 20 Chinese citizens remanded for four days in love scam probe
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: Twenty Chinese citizens have been remanded for four days to assist in investigations into a suspected love scam syndicate targeting victims in China. Magistrate Nurhanisah S. H. Sahul Hamid issued the remand order until Thursday to allow police to conduct further investigations. They are suspected of involvement in a love scam syndicate targeting victims in China using Telegram for online fraud activities.

items.title: E-hailing driver charged with attempted murder after setting woman on fire in Kepong
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 24 — An e-hailing driver has claimed trial at the Sessions Court here to an attempted murder charge after allegedly dousing a 62-year-old woman in petrol and setting her ablaze in Kepong earlier this month. Ang Kam Tong, 58, pleaded not guilty after the charge was read before Judge Surita Budin, FMT reported. Deputy Public Prosecutor Nur Shakila Shariff objected to bail, telling the court that Ang had attempted to evade arrest.

items.title: 10 injured in Subang Jaya theme park roller coaster accident
items.summary: SUBANG JAYA: Ten people were injured in a roller coaster accident at a theme park here on Saturday night. District police chief Assistant Commissioner Wan Azlan Wan Mamat said the incident occurred at 9pm and involved 22 riders, comprising Malaysians and foreign tourists aged between 11 and 44. He said 10 of the riders suffered injuries and were taken to medical facilities around Subang Jaya for treatment.

items.title: "Just come and see me," Indira's plea for missing daughter
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: For 17 years, M. Indira Gandhi has lived with the same unanswered question: where is her daughter, Prasana Diksa? After another court battle ended today, the answer remains elusive. The kindergarten teacher was visibly disappointed after the Court of Appeal dismissed her appeal in her RM100 million suit against the police and government, but stressed that the case had never been about money.

items.title: China evacuates tens of thousands as rain from Typhoon Narra lashes southwest
items.summary: BEIJING: Torrential rain triggered by Typhoon Narra caused widespread flooding across China's southwestern Guangxi region over the weekend, forcing tens of thousands of people to relocate as forecasters warned of more downpours in the days ahead. Some 54,000 people have been relocated because of the flooding, including 8,087 moved to emergency shelters, state broadcaster CCTV said. Heavy rain is expected to persist across parts of southern China through Wednesday, with areas of Guangxi, Guangdong, Hainan and Fujian forecast to receive torrential rain, CCTV said.

items.title: Narcotics policeman in Kelantan investigated over alleged affair
items.summary: State police chief Datuk Mohd Yusoff Mamat said the probe was initiated after a 30-second video clip purportedly involving the policeman went viral on social media yesterday. "The policeman's statement has also been recorded," he said when contacted. Mohd Yusoff said police would await the outcome of the internal investigation before taking further action.

items.title: Malaysia's leading index rises 1.3pct on trade, chip demand
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's leading index posted an annual growth of 1.3 per cent to 114.8 points in June, reflecting the strengthening of Malaysia's trade activities, said the Statistics Department. The index was driven by a surge in real imports of other basic precious and other non-ferrous metals (35.1 per cent) as well as real imports of semiconductors (14.2 per cent). For current economic performance, the coincident index rose 2.6 per cent year-on-year with 131.6 points underpinned by strong growth in all components, particularly the real contributions, Employees Provident Fund (16 per cent) and the volume index of retail trade (4.1 per cent).

items.title: Court of Appeal dismisses Indira Gandhi’s RM100m suit despite flagging police shortcomings
items.summary: While dismissing the appeal, a three-member bench chaired by Datuk Mohamed Zaini Mazlan highlighted material deficiencies in police records concerning efforts to execute an arrest warrant against her fugitive former husband, K. Pathmanathan, also known as Muhammad Riduan Abdullah, NST reported. Datuk Faizah Jamaludin and Datuk Mohd Radzi Abdul Hamid also sat on the bench. Delivering the unanimous decision, Faizah ruled that the available evidence failed to establish that any specific police omission directly prevented Pathmanathan’s arrest or the recovery of Prasana.

items.title: E-hailing driver charged with attempted murder after setting Kepong woman on fire
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: An e-hailing driver pleaded not guilty at the Sessions Court here today to a charge of attempting to murder a lottery outlet worker by setting her on fire, leaving her with severe injuries. According to the charge sheet, Ang is accused of attempting to murder Gan Siew Teen, 62, by dousing her with petrol and setting her alight at a lottery outlet in Taman Pusat Kepong at 7.51am on Aug 9, causing her to suffer severe third-degree burns. However, lawyer Lee Keng Fatt, representing the accused, applied for bail.

items.title: Pax Silica makes navigating global critical minerals supply war harder
items.summary: Two Asean countries, the Philippines and Singapore, had signed the US-led Pax Silica Declaration, which set up a cartel in critical minerals. To date, 25 countries have signed the Pax Silica Declaration (Pax Silica is Latin for Silicon Peace). Asean countries with known deposits of rare earth include Vietnam, Indonesia, Myanmar, Malaysia and Thailand.

items.title: Govt mulls single tax agency to streamline revenue collection
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The government is considering streamlining national revenue administration through a unified collection system, including the proposed establishment of a Single Tax Agency (STA). The proposal to consolidate the tax collection functions of the Customs Department and the Inland Revenue Board (IRB) was discussed at an enforcement and tax compliance meeting in June. The proposed integration could significantly reshape the country's revenue administration by reducing overlapping functions, improving collection efficiency, lowering administrative costs and easing taxpayers' compliance burden.

items.title: Court dismisses Indira Gandhi's RM100mil suit despite finding gaps in police evidence
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The Court of Appeal today dismissed kindergarten teacher M. Indira Gandhi's appeal to reinstate her RM100 million suit against the police and government over their alleged failure to locate her daughter, Prasana Diksa. Despite this dismissal, a three-member bench chaired by Datuk Mohamed Zaini Mazlan found material deficiencies in police evidence regarding their efforts to execute an arrest warrant against her former husband, K. Pathmanathan, also known as Muhammad Riduan Abdullah. Faizah, who read the unanimous decision, said the evidence did not establish that any particular omission by the police would have likely resulted in Pathmanathan's arrest or Prasana Diksa's recovery.

items.title: Sarawak leads haze misery as Serian hits 194, unhealthy API spreads to Selangor, Kedah, Penang
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 24 — Ten areas in four states recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 10am today, with Serian, Sarawak recording the highest reading, nearing the very unhealthy level. Other areas in the state that recorded unhealthy air quality were Kuching (176), Samarahan (172), Sri Aman (158) and Bintulu (125). A further 58 areas nationwide recorded moderate air quality.

items.title: Eight including influencer remanded over traffic stopped for race
items.summary: KULAI: A motorsports influencer was among eight suspects remanded for four days from today over a viral video showing traffic on the Second Link Expressway being stopped for an illegal race. [[nid:1517591]] All the men wore face masks, while two, including the influencer, wore hoodies. Johor police chief Datuk Ab.

items.title: Three squatter homes razed in Sentul blaze, 26‑year‑old man treated for burn injuries
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 24 — A man suffered burns to his body and legs in a fire that destroyed three squatter houses in Jalan Ismail Ghani, Kampung Kasipillay, Sentul, here early this morning. Kuala Lumpur Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) operations assistant director Ahmad Mukhlis Mukhtar said the emergency call was received at 1.15am before teams from Sentul, Hang Tuah and Gombak Selatan Fire and Rescue Stations rushed to the location. “Upon arrival of the fire brigade at the location, the fire was found to involve three semi-permanent squatter houses with a total area of 4,872 square feet.

items.title: Haze: 10 areas in four states record unhealthy API readings
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Ten areas in four states recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 10am today, with Serian, Sarawak, recording the highest reading, nearing the very unhealthy level. Other areas in the state that recorded unhealthy air quality were Kuching (176), Samarahan (172), Sri Aman (158) and Bintulu (125). A further 58 areas nationwide recorded moderate air quality.

items.title: DBKL cracks down on unlicensed entertainment outlets
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Kuala Lumpur City Hall (DBKL) has cracked down on several entertainment outlets across the capital for operating without a valid license. During a special operation conducted yesterday, DBKL targeted foreign-operated establishments and business premises that failed to comply with food establishment licensing conditions. "Three offence notices were also issued to premises operating entertainment without a license.

items.title: PA Resources's jumped 10pct following stellar earnings
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: PA Resources Bhd's shares rose nearly 10 per cent on Monday morning following a surge in its net profit for the fourth quarter. Its shares climbed 9.5 per cent to 23 sen in early trade, from 21 sen closing price last Friday, before settling at 22.5 sen at 10.30am. For the full year, its earnings climbed 10.8 per cent to RM31 million while revenue rose almost 20 per cent to RM648.6 million from RM541 million last year.

items.title: MARKET PULSE AM AUGUST 24, 2026 [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia's 30-stock index opened marginally higher, trailing Wall Street's performance despite elevated US long term yields. The key index climbed nearly two points to open at 1,738. In the crypto exchange, Bitcoin rose to RM310,615 driven by adoption growth amid US government deficits and blockchain integration.

items.title: Gen Z-inspired songs to feature in National Day celebration
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: This year's National Day celebration will feature Gen Z-inspired songs and performances alongside traditional elements as part of a human graphic presentation involving 1,500 school students. Education Ministry Sports, Co-curriculum and Arts Division director Ithnin Mahadi said the presentation would feature 16 songs spanning current Gen Z music, traditional songs and other genres. Ithnin said the new elements were expected to give this year's performance a different feel compared with last year's celebration.

items.title: Genting privatisation hinges on Resorts World New York turnaround
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The prospect of Genting Bhd making another bid to privatise Genting Malaysia Bhd (GENM) is likely to depend on whether the turnaround at Resorts World New York City (RWNYC) gains enough traction to justify taking the casino operator private, CGS International Securities Malaysia said. The renewed speculation comes after Genting retained a 73.88 per cent stake in GENM following the expiry of its unconditional mandatory takeover offer in December 2025. "In October 2025, when it launched the mandatory takeover offer of GENM at RM2.35 a share, it said it did not intend to keep the listing status of GENM," said CGS International analyst Chong Tjen-San.

items.title: NexG plunged 17pct after govt said not buying DTSB
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: NexG Bhd shares fell sharply in early trade today after the government said it would not take over Datasonic Technologies Sdn Bhd (DTSB). The counter opened at 29.5 sen, down 2.5 sen or 7.8 per cent from Friday's close of 32 sen, before falling as much as 5.5 sen or 17.2 per cent to 26.5 sen. At 10.42am, NexG was trading at 27.5 sen, down 4.5 sen or 14.1 per cent, giving the company a market capitalisation of about RM1 billion. MMAG Holdings Bhd, in which NexG holds a 9.48 per cent stake, fell half-a-sen or 17 per cent to 2.5 sen, valuing the company at RM58 million.

items.title: Melaka polls: Anwar, Amirudin meet as Pakatan weighs BN pact
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 24 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim met with Pakatan Harapan election director Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari over the weekend, with a potential electoral pact with Barisan Nasional for the next Melaka state polls believed to be high on the agenda. PH communications director Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil confirmed the meeting took place, though he noted he was not briefed on the specifics. On the BN front, chairman Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi has maintained that the coalition will not enter any automatic arrangement with Perikatan, leaving the ultimate decision to Melaka Chief Minister and state Umno-Barisan chief Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh.

items.title: Noise row in Sarawak turns violent as knife attack leaves man wounded outside Bau home
items.summary: Bau District police chief Supt Mohd Haide A. Rahman said the incident took place at around 1pm, when the complainant became involved in a heated argument with the suspect. “The victim also sustained a minor laceration to his left wrist while attempting to block the knife during the assault,” he said in a statement. Mohd Haide said the suspect had been identified and the knife had been seized.

items.title: Genting earnings seen surging on plantations, casino recovery
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: CIMB Securities Sdn Bhd has raised its 2026 and 2027 (FY26/FY27) core net profit forecasts for Genting Bhd by 14 per cent and 4.0 per cent respectively, driven largely by a brighter earnings outlook for Genting Plantations Bhd (GENP). The research house expects Genting's core net profit to rebound 212 per cent year-on-year (YoY) in FY26, supported by narrower losses at Resorts World Las Vegas (RWLV) and robust plantation earnings, partly offset by weaker contributions from Genting Malaysia Bhd (GENM) and Genting Singapore Ltd (GENS). GENS delivered a mixed performance, with EBITDA rising 12 per cent YoY and 18 per cent QoQ, while core net profit fell 4.0 per cent YoY to S$94 million (RM294 million).

items.title: Dollar trading near multi-month lows, restrained by debt nerves
items.summary: SINGAPORE: A wavering dollar teetered near multi-month lows on Monday in a market unsettled by the US Treasury's promise to buy back more long bonds, while traders awaited details of sanctions on Iran and on policy speeches this week in the US and Japan. The Australian and New Zealand dollars traded just shy of three-month highs at US$0.7171 and US$0.5979 respectively. The euro was comfortably above US$1.16 at US$1.1685 while the yen kept to the strong side of 159 per dollar.

items.title: Solehah to challenge IIUM dismissal in Industrial Court
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Academic Dr Solehah Yaacob will challenge the International Islamic University Malaysia (IIUM) over its decision to terminate her services by taking the matter to the Industrial Court. Solehah said she had rejected IIUM's offer of compensation equivalent to six months' salary following her dismissal. IIUM had previously confirmed that Solehah's service as an academic staff member ended on April 27.

items.title: Gold hits over 3-month high ahead of US inflation data, Fed chair speech
items.summary: Spot gold was up 0.5 per cent at US$4,627.42 per ounce, as of 0155 GMT, after hitting its highest level since May 15 earlier in the session. Prices gained more than five per cent last week. US gold futures edged 0.1 per cent higher to US$4,683.80.

items.title: Oil falls ahead of US announcement on new Iran sanctions
items.summary: Brent crude futures fell US$1.22, or 1.29 per cent, to US$93.17 by 0035 GMT, while US West Texas Intermediate crude was at US$85.86 a barrel, down US$1.20, or 1.38 per cent. US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, set to hold a press conference at 2pm EDT (1800 GMT) on Monday, has threatened to impose "the toughest sanctions in history" on Iran. President Donald Trump has also threatened to impose sanctions on Iran's trading partners.

items.title: Shares flat in Asia before Iran sanctions news, Nvidia results
items.summary: Analysts are generally looking for quarterly revenue to almost double to around US$92 billion, with full-year earnings guidance seen in a range of US$103 billion to US$105 billion. Brent slipped 1.0 per cent to US$93.43 ahead of the announcement, though that followed gains of 6.6 per cent last week. US crude eased 1.1 per cent to US$86.14 a barrel.

items.title: Japan's Nikkei wavers as AI stocks weigh ahead of Nvidia earnings
items.summary: Japanese government bond yields ticked higher in morning trading. The Nikkei was 0.2 per cent higher at 65,900.95 at 0156 GMT, after oscillating between gains of as much as 0.4 per cent and losses of 0.5 per cent. Most AI-related shares, which tend to be heavily weighted on the Nikkei, declined, with Fujikura losing 3.5 per cent and SoftBank Group slipping 3.3 per cent Chip-making tool manufacturers outperformed, though, with Tokyo Electron rising 2.1 per cent.

items.title: Melaka election countdown? Perikatan hints at polls within two months
items.summary: AYER KEROH, Aug 24 — Perikatan Nasional (PN) has teased a tight timeline for the Melaka state election, suggesting the polls could be held in less than two months and putting the coalition’s election machinery on high alert. PN chairman Datuk Seri Ahmad Samsuri Mokhtar warned that a 60-day window should not be mistaken for a long period, but rather viewed as a critical countdown to determine who will govern the state, NST reported. Speaking in the presence of PAS president Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang, Ahmad Samsuri, who also serves as a PAS vice-president, vowed that PN is prepared to govern Melaka regardless of the political landscape.

items.title: Mr Opposition — The legacy of Tan Chee Khoon
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 24 — A steady crowd of 150 or so were present at yesterday’s public forum marking 30 years since the death of former opposition leader Dr Tan Chee Khoon. Jointly organised by Aliran and his youngest daughter Tan Poh Lai, the event at the KLSCAH is one of three subtitled Merdeka, Multiracialism and Dissent, Without Fear or Favour. He was elected to Parliament in 1964 under the Labour Party, 1969 under Gerakan and 1974 under Pekemas.

items.title: Hadi: Perikatan and BN already in talks for Melaka state election pact
items.summary: MELAKA, Aug 24 — Perikatan Nasional (PN) and Barisan Nasional (BN) have entered negotiations to forge a cooperation pact for the upcoming Melaka state election (PRN). PAS president Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang disclosed that talks between representatives appointed by the central leadership of both coalitions kicked off three days ago, Sinar Harian reported. While acknowledging that discussions are in their infancy, Abdul Hadi noted that the initial momentum has been promising.

items.title: Housewife in her 70s tricked by ritual scam in Sibu, police confirm RM317,000 losses
items.summary: Sibu police chief ACP Abang Zainal Abidin Abang Ahmad said the local woman, in her 70s, lodged a police report yesterday over the incident, which occurred on July 19 in the Sibu Market area. He said the victim was initially approached by an unidentified woman, believed to be a Chinese national based on her accent, who asked for directions to a Chinese traditional medicine shop, allegedly to obtain medicine for her mother-in-law. Abang Zainal Abidin said the suspects then offered a protection ritual and asked the victim to hand over cash and jewellery for the purpose.

items.title: Amirudin says viral Sukma holiday poster fake, official decision based on medal tally tonight
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Aug 24 — Selangor Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari has denied the authenticity of a viral poster announcing a special public holiday to mark the state’s victory at the 2026 Malaysia Games (Sukma). Please take note and remain patient,” he said. Yesterday, state Youth, Sports, and Entrepreneurship Committee chairman Mohd Najwan Halimi was reported as saying that the state government would consider declaring a special public holiday if the Selangor contingent emerged as the overall champion at the Games.

items.title: Record-breaking crowds storm Menara Merdeka 118 for IHH Sky Race
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, August 24 — More than 8,000 athletes stormed the 118 floors of Menara Merdeka 118 over the weekend, as the IHH Sky Race returned for its second year to cement its status as Malaysia’s premier tower running event. Japanese tower runner Ryoji Watanabe claimed victory with a blistering time of 15 minutes and 38 seconds. Soh secured second place, conquering the 2,845 steps in 15 minutes and 48 seconds, while Australian Mark Bourne followed in third at 16 minutes and 33 seconds.

items.title: Kelantan police hunt depot escapees in numbered greens, warn Kota Bharu residents against direct confrontation
items.summary: “Their last known location was Bukit Tebu, Tanah Merah. The statement posted on the Kelantan Contingent Police Headquarters’ Facebook page said the fugitives comprise seven Thai nationals, one Indonesian, one Bangladeshi and one Rohingya. Information can be directed to the Tanah Merah District Control Centre at 09-955 6222 (Tanah Merah District Police Headquarters), 09-955 6223 (Tanah Merah Police Station), or via WhatsApp at 011-2955 5518.

items.title: National Housing Policy: What does the policy mean for Malaysians
items.summary: The policy proposes using more detailed local data to determine where housing is needed, expanding rental and financing options, making better use of existing housing stock and strengthening the way housing projects are approved and delivered. Here is what the policy proposes and how it helps Malaysians with housing related matters. The DRN looks to ensure housing projections at the sub-district and district level, take into account existing housing supply, vacant units, housing types, household income and price categories.

items.title: Two boys, 13 and 16, found dead after being swept away by strong currents in Sabah
items.summary: KENINGAU, Aug 23 — Two teenage boys who were reported missing after being swept away by strong currents in Sungai Pegalan, Kampung Bakti here yesterday, were found dead today. The Sabah Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) Operations Centre said the body of the first victim, Jasti Gomen, 16, was found at 10.34am, while the second victim, Khend Rommel Ponce Caceres, 13, was found at 3.55pm. “The body of the first victim was found by the Water Rescue Team (PPDA) 50 metres from the place he was reported to have been swept away, while the second victim was found 80 metres away,” the Sabah JBPM said in a statement today.

items.title: No militants have crossed into Malaysia after southern Thailand attacks, authorities say
items.summary: PASIR MAS, Aug 23 — There has been no reported attempt by militants or guerrillas from Southern Thailand to cross into Kelantan so far, following last night’s coordinated bombings and violent attacks across three southern Thai provinces. Confirming this, Southeast Brigade Commander of the General Operations Force (PGA) SAC Ahmad Radzi Hussain said border security along the Malaysia-Thailand frontier is being tightened as a precaution, with front-line personnel on high alert for any potential infiltration attempts. Meanwhile, Mohd Yusoff confirmed today that no Malaysians were caught in last night’s bombings and violence across three southern Thai provinces.

items.title: October Sarawak assembly sitting no sign of November state election, says Abdul Karim
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Aug 23 — The possibility of the Sarawak State Legislative Assembly (DUN) sitting being brought forward to October is not an indication that the next state election will be held in November, said Parti Pesaka Bumiputera Bersatu (PBB) information chief Datuk Seri Abdul Karim Rahman Hamzah. He said the DUN normally sits at least twice a year, and therefore the possible change from November to October should not be linked to speculation over the timing of the state election. Usually, the sitting is held in November.

items.title: Care should not fall on families alone, says Nancy as welfare spending hits RM728m
items.summary: KUCHING, Aug 23 — The Social Welfare Department (JKM) has spent about RM728.5 million to support the welfare of senior citizens, persons with disabilities (PwD) and chronic patients nationwide as of June this year. Women, Family and Community Development Minister Datuk Seri Nancy Shukri said the allocation was channelled through the Senior Citizen Assistance (BWE) and the Assistance for Care of Bedridden Persons with Disabilities and Bedridden Chronic Patients (BPT). “To ease the burden on families, the Social Welfare Department also assists with the care of bedridden persons with disabilities, bedridden chronic patients and non-bedridden chronic patients who meet the eligibility criteria.

items.title: Kemaman police detain man over alleged seditious Facebook post against Royal Institution and govt
items.summary: CHUKAI, Aug 23 — Police have detained a man suspected of making a seditious and insulting Facebook post against the Royal Institution, the Malaysian government and a security agency. Kemaman police chief Supt Mohd Razi Rosli said the 39-year-old man was arrested in Damansara Damai, Petaling Jaya, Selangor on Wednesday, and a mobile phone and two SIM cards were seized. Mohd Razi said the man has been remanded until Wednesday to assist in the investigation under Section 4(1) of the Sedition Act 1948 and Section 233 of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998.

items.title: Haze watch: Sungai Petani, Johan Setia worsen as five more areas in Malaysia edge towards unhealthy levels
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 23 — The haze picture shifted across peninsular Malaysia this afternoon, with Sungai Petani worsening and five other areas creeping towards unhealthy levels, while Sarawak remained the country’s worst-affected region. Creeping towards unhealthy Five locations were now hovering close to the unhealthy threshold, with Klang recording 95, Banting and Putrajaya 93 each, Bukit Rambai in Melaka 92 and Nilai in Negeri Sembilan 91. All five remained in the moderate category but were within 10 points of the unhealthy threshold.

items.title: Terengganu’s Teluk Kalong Beach hit by coal pollution again, second incident this year
items.summary: CHUKAI, Aug 23 — Teluk Kalong Beach here has once again been affected by coal pollution over the past three days, believed to have originated from a barge that broke apart near the beach last January. He said the beach had experienced similar pollution last January following a coal spill from a barge, although cleanup operations were subsequently carried out by the parties involved. “I hope the authorities will immediately carry out cleanup operations to remove the coal debris, ensuring the cleanliness of the beach as well as the safety and well-being of fishermen and visitors,” he told Bernama when met at Teluk Kalong Beach today.

items.title: Zahid: Malaysia should build full ecosystem to lead global Muslim travel economy
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 23 — Malaysia must move beyond being the world’s leading Muslim-friendly destination and become a global hub for the Muslim travel economy, Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said. He said the country should build an ecosystem that connects tourism with halal innovation, trade, technology and local enterprises, while creating opportunities for entrepreneurs, small businesses and communities. Tourism should therefore be viewed as an economic multiplier,” he said.

items.title: MCMC, Selangor to expand filtered internet service to public premises and private institutions, says exco
items.summary: PETALING JAYA, Aug 23 — The Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC), in collaboration with the Selangor state government, plans to expand its filtered internet service to public premises and private higher learning institutions (IPTS). He said content filtering was important to ensure digital access was not misused during important activities such as prayers and learning sessions. On cyber threats, Mohammad Fahmi said 35,073 online scam cases were recorded as of June, involving losses of RM951.7 million, with investment scams accounting for RM413.8 million.

items.title: Selangor may declare holiday if host contingent emerge overall Sukma champions, says exco
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Aug 23 — The Selangor government will consider declaring an occasional holiday if the host contingent emerge overall champions at the ongoing Malaysia Games (SUKMA) 2026. State Youth, Sports and Entrepreneurship Committee chairman Mohd Najwan Halimi said the matter would only be announced after the medal tally is finalised, with the Selangor contingent looking well placed to end the Games on a high. Najwan said that as of 2.50 pm today, Selangor had collected 85 gold medals, with the latest contributed by, among others, the women’s Mobile Legends: Bang Bang (MLBB) esports team, women’s 3m springboard diving, women’s singles table tennis and men’s singles lawn bowls.

items.title: Got 20,000 tech engineers, but where are the investors? Jerejak may have the answer, says Bayan Baru MP
items.summary: Bayan Baru MP Sim Tze Tzin said the proposed 32-hectare development could bring venture capitalists, private equity firms, bankers and technology investors closer to the engineers driving Penang’s semiconductor industry, The Star reported. Sim said Penang has about 20,000 integrated circuit design engineers, many of whom remain salaried employees because they lack investors to help them establish their own companies. Sim, who lived in Silicon Valley for six years, said regular interaction between engineers, entrepreneurs and investors could help generate new ideas and spur the growth of Penang’s technology sector.

items.title: PM approves additional RM1m for Hindu crematorium project in Bagan, says PHEB
items.summary: BUTTERWORTH, Aug 23 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has approved an additional RM1 million allocation to the Penang State Hindu Endowments Board (PHEB) for the construction of a modern Hindu crematorium in Bagan here, said PHEB chairman RSN Rayer. He said the additional allocation brought the total funding for the project to RM2.5 million, up from the RM1.5 million previously approved by Anwar. He said the original RM1.5 million allocation was found to be insufficient to implement the project, which is much needed by the Hindu community, particularly in Seberang Perai.

items.title: Post-mortem shows 11-year-old tahfiz participant found in Lenggeng pond died from drowning, police say no signs of abuse
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Aug 23 — An 11-year-old boy who was found in a pond near a foundation centre in Kampung Kapal, Lenggeng early today died from drowning, resulting in a lack of oxygen, police said. “External and internal examinations of the victim’s body also found no other injuries or signs indicating abuse,” the senior police officer was quoted as saying. The boy had been reported missing while taking part in a tahfiz – a Quran memorisation – programme before he was found in a weak condition in a pond near the site.

items.title: After southern Thailand blasts, Wisma Putra tells Malaysians to think twice before crossing border
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 23 — Malaysians planning to travel to or cross into southern Thailand have been urged to exercise heightened caution and postpone non-essential trips following a wave of bomb blasts and other attacks across the region last night. The Foreign Ministry, also called Wisma Putra, said no Malaysians had been reported affected by the incidents in Yala, Pattani and Narathiwat, but advised those residing in, travelling through or planning trips to the affected areas to remain vigilant and follow local security instructions. “Malaysians residing in, travelling through, or intending to travel to and from the southern border provinces of Thailand are strongly advised to exercise heightened caution, remain vigilant, and strictly observe all safety advisories, curfews, and security instructions implemented by local authorities,” it said in a media advisory today.

items.title: IIUM ends ties with academic behind controversial Roman-Malay shipbuilding claim
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 23 — International Islamic University Malaysia (IIUM) has confirmed that controversial academic Solehah Yaacob is no longer with the university, months after she drew public scrutiny over claims that ancient Romans learned shipbuilding from Malays and that meteor activity may explain Kedah’s iron ore deposits. The university said Solehah was also barred from using any official title, position or affiliation linking her to IIUM in promotional materials, media reports, publications, advertisements, social media content, publicity materials or other forms of public dissemination. IIUM said the clarification was necessary to prevent confusion over Solehah’s status and protect the university’s institutional integrity in academic representation.
